recipes.name: Butterscotch Bread Pudding
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) loaf day-old bread, torn into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine bread, milk, sugar, butter, eggs, vanilla and butterscotch chips; mixture should be the consistency of oatmeal. Pour into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven 1 hour, until nearly set. (It should have a "thigh wiggle" or wiggle as much as a well endowed thigh.) Serve warm or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Butterscotch Bread Pudding
raw_recipe.description: Butterscotch chips and brown sugar are the characteristic ingredients in this baked bread pudding.

video.description: When you’re craving a rich, soulful dessert that’s simple to make, indulge in this fabulous recipe. Tear a loaf of day-old bread into bite-size pieces and top with butterscotch chips. Then dowse everything with a quick custard of eggs, milk, melted butter, brown sugar and vanilla. Bake for an hour, then serve warm—or cold, if you wish--it’s delicious either way. A dusting of powdered sugar or a drizzle of whisky sauce is a delightful finishing touch.

review.reviewBody: This was the best bread pudding I've ever made OR tasted. However, I did change a few things: Instead of 4 cups of milk I replaced with 2 cups of whipping cream and 2 cups of half-n-half. I also added salt and cinnamon to taste and since I'm not a huge fan of butterscotch I did half butterscotch chips and half white chocoloate chips. Nestle works great. And instead of regular loaf bread, I bought French baguette style bread. I also baked mine for way over the recommended 45 minutes..more like 1 hour and 30 miuntes. I don't like soupy bread pudding in the middle so I cooked mine until it was more solid. Let me tell you this bread pudding was so crispy, buttery and delicious that it was hard to share. I ate some for breakfast lunch and dinner!!

Great recipe. I only used 1/4 cup of butterscotch chips because I didn't want it too sweet. Even so, may reduce the brown sugar by 1/4 cup and eliminate the butterscotch chips altogether. I used a tin of evaporated milk (2 cups) and then 2 cups of whole milk. The consistency was great. I divided the mixture in half and baked in 8 in square pans. I only baked one for about 30 minutes and the other for 45 minutes. I actually preferred the one baked for 30 mins because it was moister but my son liked the one baked longer. Either way, this is a great recipe and is now my go-to recipe for bread pudding.

Fabulous recipe! I was looking for a recipe to use up some 2 day old homemade donuts (I really didn’t want to throw those out!) but I didn’t have any buttersccotch chips. Noticing from other reviews how versatile this recipe was, I decided to try it. I used 1 medium apple chopped fine instead of butterscotch chips and sprinkled the batter with cinnamon after I poured it into the pan. Worried that it might not have enough flavour or sweetness I decided to make a brandy sauce, just in case. (For that I used 1/2 cup of butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup heavy cream and 1/3 cup brandy - melt over low-med heat til bubbly at the edges.) I needn’t have worried - the sauce is very nice but the pudding is fabulous with or without it. My husband and son RAVED about this dessert. Definitely keeping this recipe!

Best I’ve ever tasted! I made it with a mixture of milk, half-and-half and a little bit of heavy cream, but since I didn’t have butterscotch chips on hand I used caramel baking bits. The biggest change I made though was using the wonderful sourdough bread my nephew had made me a couple of days before Christmas. (It made wonderful French Toast, too!) I also had to bake it about 25 minutes longer, but it has a beautifully crunch on the edge!

This is delicious!!! Per other reviews I only used 1 cup of brown sugar and that was plenty. Also, used 1 cup of coconut almond milk, 1/2 cup of heavy cream, and 2.5 cups of 2% milk. Only had about a 1/2 cup of butterscotch chips but that worked. This is a keeper!

Easy to make and tasted awesome. I needed to get ready of old and expired milk (Not Sour) and hot dog buns (No mold, getting stale. I used chocolate chips instead of butterscotch chips. I hate wasting food and throwing it out. I used Cristco in the pan and the pudding did not stick.

The basic recipe was great, I substituted the butterscotch chips for chopped dates and almond slivers equaling 1 cup, the milk to cups whole milk and one cup half and half. The baking time is 1 hr. and 30 minutes. The pudding was moist and crunchy from not only the outer crust but also the almonds added. It is very sweet, so if you don't want it so sweet cut down on the brown sugar.

DEELISH! Only changes I made were to use one loaf French bread, one tablespoon cinnamon, and an extra egg. I also used half Ghiradelli caramel chips, half Nestle butterscotch chips. Cooking time for me was 1 hr 20 min. I let cool a bit and then served with Vanilla ice cream, sprinkle of cinnamon, and a little drizzle of Ghiradelli caramel sauce. Soo good and rich!
I use dinner rolls instead of bread and for the " milk products" I replaced all with half and half. I used granulated sugar instead of brown sugar.

This was very good. I read several reviews before making this. I cut the brown sugar in half and even though I enjoy sweet desserts I found that to be plenty. Because several people mentioned that this seemed "wet", I only used 3 cups of milk. I cooked this on high for 3 hours in my crock pot. Maybe because the crock pot uses a lid, the pudding turned out really moist and tasty with only 3 cups of milk. My bread was very dry before assembling this so I don't think I would ever need more milk. Because of changing the amounts of sugar and milk, I rate this a 4. Will definitely make this again. My bread was multigrain/wheat and we still enjoyed this.
Really delicious!! I cooked some thick cut bacon, cooked it till just crispy and sprinkled on top. salty and sweet, it was really nice on my brunch table. I will be making this again.
Made it with day old croissants. Amazing.
This was so incredibly good. Made it for Thanksgiving. Used croissants like someone mentioned in comments. I think the only change I did was using a full tablespoon of vanilla extract.
Great recipe! I did cook it a little longer. It ended up with a chewy almost toffee like top. Excellent flavor.
I made this recipe and used walnut rasin bread and 1 1/2 of sugar and it was delicious. My boyfriend ate almost the entire pan by himself.
Absolutely delicious!! I may use half sugar and make a caramel sauce next time.
I have made this several times. I always get asked to make it for Holiday get togethers. One time I substituted Butterfingers for the butterscotch chips. Both are very yummy

Very good! A restaurant chain I worked for used to use leftover cinnamon rolls to its bread pudding recipe, so like SethParker, I made this with cinnamon bread. Also, as much as I love butter, I'd cut the amount in half next time. I think if the brown sugar was swapped out with granulated sugar & caramel chips for the butterscotch chips, it would be a terrific "Caramel Bread Pudding."
Delicious, but very sweet.

I made it the 1st time just to see how it tasted and gave some to my daughter and her family and they loved it! So I made 2 more batches cuz it was a “Win Win” with the folks! I made it with a twist... I added half croissants and half French bread! Yum yum!
